column1: divulge§Nothing in the file divulges who authorized the payment.§卷宗里没有任何内容**透露**是谁批准了这笔付款。
docile§A docile audience asks no questions and learns nothing.§**温顺**的听众不提问，也学不到东西。
doctrinaire§The doctrinaire wing lost the vote and kept the argument.§**教条**派输掉了表决，却保住了话语。
dogmatic§Be dogmatic about evidence and flexible about conclusions.§在证据上要**严格**，在结论上要灵活。
dogmatist§A dogmatist and a skeptic can share a reading list.§**独断论者**与怀疑论者可以共用一份书单。
dominance§Dominance in one market rarely transfers to the next.§在一个市场的**优势**很少能带到下一个市场。
dominant§The dominant wind here comes from the southwest.§这里的**主导**风来自西南。
dominate§Two families dominated the town council for a century.§两个家族**主宰**了镇议会一个世纪。
dormant§A dormant clause was revived after ninety years.§一条**沉睡**的条款在九十年后被重新启用。
doubtful§He looked doubtful and signed the form anyway.§他**一脸怀疑**，还是签了表格。
dowager§The dowager's letters are the best source for the period.§这位**孀居贵妇**的信件是那个时期最好的史料。
downplay§Do not downplay a risk to make a schedule work.§不要为了赶进度而**淡化**风险。
dramatize§There is no need to dramatize what the numbers already say.§数字已经说明的事，没必要再**戏剧化**。
drench§A drenching rain saved the crop and ruined the fete.§一场**倾盆大雨**救了庄稼，毁了庆典。
drub§He took the drubbing well and came back the next season.§他坦然接受了**惨败**，第二个赛季又回来了。
dual§She holds dual citizenship and votes in neither country.§她拥有**双重**国籍，两个国家都不投票。
dubious§I am dubious about any figure that ends in three zeros.§任何以三个零结尾的数字我都**心存怀疑**。
dumbfound§He stood dumbfounded in front of a door that would not open.§他**呆呆地**站在一扇打不开的门前。
dupe§The dupe in this story is the reader, not the buyer.§这个故事里**被骗的**是读者，不是买家。
duplication§Duplication in the catalogue means two copies or two mistakes.§目录中的重复要么意味着两个**副本**，要么意味着两处错误。
duplicity§Duplicity requires a good memory, which is why it usually fails.§**口是心非**需要好记性，这正是它通常失败的原因。
durability§Durability was designed in; charm arrived by accident.§**耐用**是设计出来的，魅力是偶然得来的。
duration§The duration of the effect is measured in minutes, not hours.§这种效应的**持续时间**以分钟计，而非小时。
dwarf§A dwarf star can outlive every giant in the sky.§**矮星**可以比天上所有的巨星活得更久。
dwindle§Daylight dwindles by four minutes a day in October.§十月里日照每天**减少**四分钟。
earthy§His earthy humor did not survive the translation.§他那种**质朴**的幽默在翻译中丢失了。
ebb§They waited for the ebb before rowing across.§他们等**退潮**之后才划船渡过。
ebullient§An ebullient preface introduces a very sober book.§一篇**热情洋溢的**序言引出的是一本极其冷静的书。
eccentric§The orbit is eccentric, which is why the seasons are uneven.§这条轨道是**偏心**的，所以四季长短不均。
economic§Economic history explains the street plan better than any battle.§**经济史**比任何战役都更能解释这里的街道格局。
economical§She is economical with words and generous with time.§她**言语精简**，时间上却很慷慨。
economize§Economize on meetings, not on proofreading.§**该省的**是会议，不是校对。
edible§The berries are edible but not worth the walk.§这些浆果**可以吃**，却不值得走那么远。
edify§A well-kept archive edifies without saying anything.§一座维护良好的档案馆无声地**启迪**着人。
efface§He effaced himself so thoroughly that the credit went elsewhere.§他把自己**隐去**得太彻底，功劳记到了别人头上。
effective§The rule became effective on the first of April.§这条规定自四月一日起**生效**。
efficacious§An efficacious remedy for boredom is a difficult book.§治疗无聊的**有效**办法是一本难读的书。
efficient§Efficient is not the same as fast; it means less wasted.§**高效**不等于快，它意味着浪费更少。
effrontery§The effrontery of the reply was almost admirable.§这份回复的**厚颜**几乎令人佩服。
effusive§Effusive praise in a preface tells you about the friendship.§序言里**溢美之词**说明的是交情。
egalitarian§An egalitarian seating plan changed how the meetings went.§一种**平等**的座位安排改变了会议的进行方式。
egoism§Egoism explains the memoir; ambition explains the career.§**自我主义**解释了这本回忆录，野心解释了这段事业。
egotistical§An egotistical narrator can still be a reliable one.§**自我本位的**叙述者仍可能是可靠的。
egregious§Egregious as the error was, it changed nothing.§这个错误虽然**离谱**，却什么也没改变。
elaborate§An elaborate excuse is less convincing than a short one.§**精心编造**的借口不如简短的可信。
elate§He was elated by an outcome he had privately predicted.§他为一个自己私下早已预料的结果而**兴高采烈**。
elation§Elation and exhaustion arrived in the same hour.§**兴奋**与疲惫在同一小时到来。
elegance§There is an elegance in the way the roof sheds water.§这个屋顶排水的方式有一种**优雅**。
elementary§Elementary questions are the ones experts stop asking.§最**基本的**问题正是专家不再问的问题。
elevate§The platform elevates the speaker and separates her from the room.§讲台**抬高**了讲话者，也把她与全场隔开。
eliminate§Eliminate the impossible and check what is left twice.§**排除**不可能的，然后把剩下的核对两遍。
elitist§It is not elitist to expect people to read the footnotes.§期待人们读脚注并不是**精英主义**。
elliptical§The moon's path is elliptical, not circular.§月球的轨道是**椭圆的**，不是圆形的。
elocutionist§Every elocutionist of the period taught the same six vowels.§那个时期的每位**演说教师**都教同样的六个元音。
eloquent§The empty chair was more eloquent than the speech.§那把空椅子比演讲**更有说服力**。
elude§The name eluded her until she was halfway home.§那个名字直到她走到半路**才想起来**。
elusive§Precision here is elusive and worth pursuing anyway.§这里的精确**难以捉摸**，却依然值得追求。
embarrassment§An embarrassment of good candidates is a real problem.§**好人选太多**也是个实实在在的难题。
embellish§He embellished the account until it was unusable as evidence.§他把这段叙述**添油加醋**到无法作为证据。
embellishment§Strip the embellishment and the argument stands.§去掉**修饰**，论点依然成立。
embitter§Nothing embitters like being right too early.§没有什么比过早正确更让人**心生怨恨**。
emblem§The key on the seal is an emblem of the port's old privileges.§印章上的钥匙是这个港口旧日特权的**象征**。
embodiment§The building is the embodiment of a rule nobody wrote down.§这座建筑是一条无人写下的规则的具体**化身**。
embolden§A first acceptance emboldens a writer for about a week.§第一次被录用能让作者**胆气壮**上大约一周。
embrace§The two shores embrace a harbor a mile across.§两岸**环抱**着一个一英里宽的港湾。
embroil§Do not get embroiled in a dispute over the punctuation.§不要**卷入**一场关于标点的争执。
eminent§An eminent name on the cover sells a book nobody finishes.§封面上一个**显赫的**名字能卖出一本没人读完的书。
emotional§The argument is emotional, which does not make it wrong.§这个论证带着**情绪**，但这并不使它变错。
